variables.meaning: temperature, the quantity measured by a thermometer
a temperature on the Celsius scale, on which water freezes at 0 °C and boils at 100 °C
a temperature on the Fahrenheit scale, on which water freezes at 32 °F and boils at 212 °F
a temperature on the Kelvin scale, the absolute scale whose zero is absolute zero and whose unit is the SI unit of temperature
the pressure of a gas kept at constant volume, which falls in a straight line with temperature and extrapolates to zero at −273.15 °C
the change in length of a body when its temperature changes
the length of the body before the temperature change, such as the 1275 m span of the Golden Gate Bridge
the change in temperature, which is the same number in kelvins and in degrees Celsius
the coefficient of linear expansion, the change in length per unit length per degree, which depends on the material and varies slightly with temperature
the change in area of a plate or of a hole when its temperature changes
the area before the temperature change
the change in volume of a body, or of the gasoline and the tank that holds it, when its temperature changes
the volume before the temperature change
the coefficient of volume expansion, the change in volume per unit volume per degree, which is very nearly three times the coefficient of linear expansion
the pressure created when a body that would have expanded is held at its original volume, which is the thermal stress
the bulk modulus of the material, which relates a change in volume to the pressure that produces it
the original volume of the gasoline before it is heated
the force on the walls of the container, which divided by their area is the pressure
the absolute pressure of the gas
the volume the gas occupies
the number of atoms and molecules in the gas, which is the same for every kind of gas at the same pressure, volume and temperature
the Boltzmann constant, which relates energy to temperature and has the value 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J/K
the absolute temperature of the gas, which must be in kelvins in the ideal gas law
the initial pressure of the gas in the tire, before its temperature rises
the final pressure of the gas after its temperature has risen at constant volume
the initial absolute temperature of the gas
the final absolute temperature of the gas
the number of moles of gas
Avogadro's number, the number of particles in one mole of any substance, 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹
the universal gas constant, the product of Avogadro's number and the Boltzmann constant, 8.31 J/(mol·K)
the molar mass of a substance, the mass of one mole of it, such as 28.8 g/mol for dry air
the pressure of the gas, the average force per unit area its molecules exert on the walls of its volume
the volume of gas in the container
the number of molecules in the container
the mass of one molecule, found by dividing the molar mass by Avogadro's number
the average of the molecular speed squared
the average translational kinetic energy of a molecule, which is the thermal energy and is proportional to the absolute temperature
the Boltzmann constant
the absolute temperature of the gas
the root-mean-square speed of the molecules, the square root of the average of the speed squared
the most probable speed, at the peak of the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution, which is less than the rms speed
the component of a molecule's velocity perpendicular to the wall, which is reversed by the collision
the change in a molecule's momentum when it bounces off the wall, 2mv_x
the average time between a molecule's collisions with one wall, the time to cross the box and back
the force the wall exerts on a molecule during a collision, and by Newton's third law the force the molecule exerts on the wall
the length of the box, so that a molecule travels 2l between collisions with the same wall
the area of the wall, so that the volume of the box is Al
the lower of two temperatures at which the distribution of molecular speeds is drawn
the higher temperature, at which the distribution is shifted to higher speeds and broadened
the pressure of the substance, one axis of a PV diagram and of a phase diagram
the volume of the substance, the other axis of a PV diagram
the temperature of the substance, fixed along an isotherm and one axis of a phase diagram
the number of molecules, held fixed along an isotherm
the Boltzmann constant
the critical temperature, above which the liquid phase cannot exist at any pressure
the vapor pressure of water at the given temperature, which is the partial pressure of water vapor when the air is saturated
the number of moles of water vapor
the volume the vapor occupies
the universal gas constant, 8.31 J/(mol·K)
the absolute temperature of the air
the vapor density, the mass of water vapor per cubic meter of air, which at saturation is the saturation vapor density of Table 13.5
